regex-tester.metaDescription: Test JavaScript regex live: see all matches, capture groups, and highlighted text as you type. Free, no signup, runs in your browser.
regex-tester.keywords: regex tester, regular expression tester, test regex online, javascript regex, regex match
regex-tester.quickAnswer: Type a regular expression and test text, and this tool instantly shows every match: the matched text, its position, and any capture groups. Matches are highlighted in the text, flags like case-insensitive or multiline can be toggled, and invalid patterns show a clear error message.
keyFacts: Regular expressions describe text patterns; this tool uses the JavaScript regex engine.
The g flag is always on, so every match in the text is found, not just the first.
Parentheses create capture groups whose matched parts are listed separately.
An invalid pattern shows the exact engine error instead of failing silently.
Matching runs locally on every keystroke with no delay or server round-trip.
howTo: Type your pattern in the pattern field (for example, \d+ for digits).
Toggle flags: i for case-insensitive, m for multiline, s for dot-all, u for unicode.
Paste or type the text to test in the test area.
Read the match count, highlighted matches, and capture group details.
Refine the pattern until it matches exactly what you want.
regex-tester.formula:
Pattern: \b[A-Z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Z0-9.-]+\.[A-Z]{2,}\b  (email, case-insensitive)
Test: "mail me at test@example.com"
Match #1: test@example.com at index 11
regex-tester.workedExample:
Pattern: \b[A-Z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Z0-9.-]+\.[A-Z]{2,}\b with the i flag
Test text: "Contact support@jaurtools.com or sales@jaurtools.com."
Result: 2 matches — support@jaurtools.com at index 8 and sales@jaurtools.com at index 32.
"not-an-email" does not match because it has no @ and domain part.
benefits: Instant feedback while you build complex patterns.
Capture groups listed per match for debugging.
Clear error messages for invalid patterns.
No data leaves the browser; test sensitive text safely.
limitations: Uses the JavaScript regex engine; PCRE-only features like lookbehind limits differ.
Catastrophic backtracking on huge inputs can freeze the tab briefly.
Maximum 200 matches are listed to keep the page responsive.
Empty matches are marked but do not advance highlighting visually.

faqs.a: JavaScript (ECMAScript). Most common syntax works the same, but some PCRE features like atomic groups are not supported.
Toggle the i flag. With it on, [a-z] also matches A-Z, and literal text ignores case.
Parts of the pattern in parentheses. Each match lists what each group captured, useful for extracting pieces like area codes from phone numbers.

faqs.q: Why does my pattern show an error?
faqs.a: Unbalanced parentheses or brackets, a trailing backslash, or an invalid quantifier cause engine errors. The message names the exact problem.
Yes. Paste multiline text and toggle the m flag so ^ and $ match line starts and ends instead of the whole text.
